output.summary: The run is VALID with COMPLETE analysis coverage. Both the reference and evaluation windows report verdict NO_POLICY (no applicable business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla for the windows), so no PASS/FAIL gate was evaluated. Transaction metrics show error_count 0, p50 latency 201-204 ms, p95 235-239 ms, and a constant load target of 20 requests/s. All 16 correlation pairs were tested in the evaluation window; 15 are BELOW_EFFECT / NOT_SELECTED. The sole selected correlation candidate is pair-14 (resource-14), status CANDIDATE, best_lag_ms -10000, best_lag_rho -0.487, Holm-adjusted p 0.016, uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED. Because clock alignment is not verified by core and the load control was constant (dropped as CONSTANT_CONTROL), this candidate is a stored partial correlation to investigate, not a proven cause. The deterministic NO_POLICY verdict is preserved.

hypotheses.observation: In the evaluation window, correlation pair-14 (resource-14) is CANDIDATE and is the only pair selected by the headline selection (status SELECTED, holm_adjusted_p_value 0.016, max_p_value 0.001, best_lag_ms -10000, best_lag_rho -0.487). It is the single correlation_candidate finding; the other 15 pairs are BELOW_EFFECT / NOT_SELECTED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Resource-14 utilization ratio may be inversely related to response_time_p95_ms at a -10 s lag, but clock alignment is not verified by core and the target load control was dropped as CONSTANT_CONTROL, so this is a hypothesis only, not a proven cause.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment between load generator and resource telemetry; overlay and inspect the resource-14 series against p95 latency in the evaluation window; rerun the analysis.

hypotheses.observation: Several pairs attain their best rho at the extremes of the scanned lag range: pair-03 at -10000 ms, pair-10 at +10000 ms, pair-12 at -10000 ms, and the selected pair-14 at -10000 ms; pair-04 and pair-09 also sit near the edges (-9000 / +9000 ms).
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A best lag at the scan boundary may mean the true optimum lies outside the [-10000, +10000] ms range, or the extreme values could be artifacts of an unverified clock relationship between the telemetry sources.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock alignment first, then extend the lag scan range and inspect each lag profile shape instead of relying on a single best value.

hypotheses.observation: The target series is constant at 20 requests/s in both the reference and evaluation windows (statistics show min/mean/median/max = 20 and std = 0), and every correlation pair reports controls_dropped ['target'] with reason CONSTANT_CONTROL and controls_used [].
hypotheses.possible_explanation: With a flat load target, the analysis cannot partial out load-driven effects, so the selected candidate is an uncontrolled partial correlation and its strength may be inflated or spurious.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun with a non-constant load profile (e.g., steps or ramps) so the load control can be used, and compare the pair-14 result between profiles.

hypotheses.observation: The reference and evaluation window policy summaries both report business_verdict NO_POLICY, resource_verdict NO_POLICY, and verdict NO_POLICY; the facts also state policy_verdict NO_POLICY.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No applicable business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla covered these windows, so the product reports NO_POLICY; healthy-looking transaction metrics do not make this a PASS and the verdict is independent of run health.
hypotheses.recommended_check: If a pass/fail gate is required, add applicable business policy rules and resource rules with effect: sla for the windows, then rerun the analysis.

hypotheses.observation: Overall, reference, and evaluation metric summaries report error_count 0 with p50 latency 201-204 ms and p95 235-239 ms, while the diagnostic summary reports anomalies_tested 0 and episodes_reported 0.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The run appears clean, but zero errors and zero anomaly episodes do not prove stability, spare capacity, low load, or absence of a problem; the flat 20 requests/s target is the configured load, not evidence of low load.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compare achieved throughput against the 20 requests/s target, review per-transaction and generator logs, and use a dedicated capacity or soak test if headroom conclusions are needed.

hypotheses.observation: All 16 correlation pairs and the diagnostic summary have uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED, and every pair has sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null; the selected candidate likewise has uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The candidate was selected via the mbb-lag-max-holm.v1 bootstrap without an estimated uncertainty or sensitivity, so its magnitude should not be treated as a measured effect size or confidence.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Rerun in an analysis mode that estimates uncertainty/sensitivity if the product supports it; otherwise treat the candidate as a flagged lead for manual review.

recommendations.action: Verify clock alignment/synchronization between the load generator and resource telemetry before interpreting any lag, including the candidate's best_lag_ms -10000.
recommendations.rationale: The resource binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core; unverified clocks cannot support lead/lag ordering or a temporal causal hypothesis.

recommendations.action: Keep the NO_POLICY verdict unchanged; do not present it as PASS or FAIL. If a gate is needed, configure applicable business policy rules and resource rules with effect: sla covering the windows, then rerun.
recommendations.rationale: Product semantics report NO_POLICY when no applicable rule exists; healthy metrics and a rerun do not turn NO_POLICY into PASS.

recommendations.action: Inspect the resource-14 series, the generator's resource series, and the pair-14 lag profile in the evaluation window; rerun with a healthy generator and a non-constant load profile.
recommendations.rationale: The only selected candidate (pair-14) is a partial correlation with the target control dropped (CONSTANT_CONTROL) and no clock verification; confirmation requires a usable load control.

recommendations.action: When reviewing metrics, compare counts only within the same scope and window (overall run, reference window, and evaluation window are separate denominators).
recommendations.rationale: Overall (7200 samples, throughput denominator 360233), reference (2400/120000), and evaluation (4800/240000) are different quantities; differing numbers across scopes are not inconsistencies.

recommendations.action: Rerun the correlation analysis with uncertainty/sensitivity estimation if supported, or gather additional runs before acting on pair-14.
recommendations.rationale: Uncertainty is NOT_ESTIMATED for all pairs and diagnostic outputs, and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps is null for every pair; the candidate is a flagged lead, not a measured effect.

caveats: Clock alignment is not verified by core (clock_alignment: not_verified_by_core); lag values such as best_lag_ms -10000 for pair-14 cannot support temporal lead/lag or causal ordering.
The load target was constant at 20 requests/s in both windows and was dropped as CONSTANT_CONTROL from every pair, so no load partialing was applied to the selected candidate.
All correlation outputs carry uncertainty NOT_ESTIMATED and sensitivity_without_achieved_rps null; Holm-adjusted selection is a multiple-testing decision, not an effect-size or confidence estimate.
The verdict NO_POLICY for both windows means no applicable rule was evaluated; it is neither PASS nor FAIL and does not indicate stability or spare capacity.
Zero errors, zero anomaly episodes (anomalies_tested 0, episodes_reported 0), and zero missing resource cells do not prove stability, spare capacity, or absence of a problem.

The candidate finding exists only for the evaluation window; the reference window (120 cells) and evaluation window (240 cells) have different lengths and denominators, so cross-scope comparisons are not valid.
Capacity bounds, knees, and generator guards were not part of the evidence; no claim about headroom or capacity is made.
